notes: Use Harvard referencing throughout your work.

The handbook lists 150 independent-study hours and one four-hour teaching session each week for 12 weeks. Check your personal timetable for class times and rooms.

The supplied Assignment 2 proposal template provides sections for the problem, purpose, assumptions/hypotheses, collection and analysis methods, validation and ethics. It includes an ethics application; approval is required before approaching participants or collecting data.

Week 3 independent study: complete Introduction to Referencing plus three other Learning Skills Hub modules; record why you chose them and what you learned. The slides say for next week without an exact submission date.

Assessment 1 feedback dates conflict: the new brief says 7 December 2026, while the handbook says 3 December. Confirm with the module team. The submission deadline remains 12 November 2026 at 14:00 UK time.

Assessment 1 Part A: 1,100-word literature review of a chosen computing topic; evaluate qualitative, quantitative and mixed methods. The brief asks for 4-6 academic articles plus relevant reputable sources and synthesis rather than article-by-article summaries.

Assessment 1 Part B: 500-word-equivalent analysis using the supplied dataset in R, presented in at most 15 PowerPoint slides with scripted speaker notes. Tasks cover means/standard deviations, histograms and separate box plots for the under-four-hour variables, and time trends for over-four-hour waiting.

Assessment 1 packaging needs clarification: the task specifies a report plus PowerPoint, but Submission Guidelines also call for a single 1,600-word critical review report. Confirm the required file arrangement before submission.

Assessment 1 rubric: academic practice 30%; information gathering/processing 15%; evaluation of process and information/data 15%; analysis 10%; conclusions 10%; visual presentation 10%; referencing 10%. Use the brief and its AIAS Level 2 declaration requirements.

notes: Assessment 1 dates conflict: the brief gives 16 November 2026 and feedback 7 December; the handbook and introduction slides give 11 November and feedback 2 December. Confirm with the module lead. No submission time is provided. Assessment 2 remains 6 January 2027, with feedback 27 January.
Use Harvard referencing throughout your work.
Both assessments are AIAS Level 2: AI planning. Include the required declaration and follow the individual assessment brief.
The handbook lists one four-hour session per week for 12 weeks and 150 hours of independent study. Check your personal timetable for teaching times.
Teaching combines lectures and practical workshops. The indicative sequence covers entity relationships, logical modelling, the relational model, normalisation and RDBMS architecture.

Arrange a meeting with the module lead between 26 and 30 October 2026 to review your draft logical data model (LDM). Contact the module lead when you have a viable draft. The meeting time must be arranged individually.
Groups of 5-6 students are to be assigned by Week 3. You can begin reviewing requirements before your group is allocated.
Complete all six SQL workbooks before starting Assessment 2. Assessment 2 requires a personal reflection on how the workbooks supported your implementation.

Each assessment requires an individual peer review/reflection form as well as the group submission. Missing the individual form counts as non-submission for that student. Confirm the Assessment 1 deadline because the sources disagree.

Assessment 1 practises requirements analysis, an annotated logical data model and evidence of normalisation to at least 3NF, with a report evaluating the design against client needs. Rubric: requirements 20%, modelling 30%, approach 25%, evaluation 15%, presentation 10%.
Assessment 2 assesses implementation scripts, data/report queries, planning, testing and evaluation. Rubric: database creation 25%, user reports 20%, planning 20%, testing 15%, evaluation 20%.

Brief wording needs clarification: the cover tables refer to individual reports (and website files in Assessment 2), while the main instructions describe group database work. Follow the module team's clarification. Assessment 1 also describes the review meeting as weeks beginning 26 and 30 October; the introduction slides say between those dates. Confirm the appointment window.

The supplied blank Group Contract Template asks the team to agree participation, communication, meetings, conduct, conflict handling and deadlines. Agree these together; no submission date is stated in the template.
The normalisation deck is named Week_6_Normalisation but stored in Week 5; its new revision is grouped under Week 5 to match the folder.

Normalisation slide clarification: slides 28 and 43 describe a single-column key as a 2NF requirement. In the general relational definition, composite keys are allowed: 2NF rules out partial dependencies of non-prime attributes on candidate keys. Confirm any separate assessment-specific key convention with your lecturer. The deck states 3NF is the minimum assessment target (slide 43). Reference: https://mariadb.com/docs/general-resources/database-theory/database-normalization/database-normalization-2nd-normal-form
